analysis.title: Eq Positioning and Key Levels
key_insights: GS CTA baseline flow forecasts point to about $23bn of global equity selling over the next week on a flat tape. North America accounts for nearly $36bn of selling, nearly all of it in SPX.
GS Prime Brokerage shows global equities net sold (-1.0 SDs 1-year) with de-grossing accelerating (-0.8 SDs 1-year, largest dollar de-grossing since July). Long sales outpaced short covers 5 to 1.

Info Tech was by far the most net sold global and US sector this week, net sold across all regions, with long and short sales at 2.2 to 1. In % terms the selling was about on par with mid-October and Sep '24, the largest net selling weeks on record since 2016. 4 of the top 5 net selling weeks in global Info Tech on record fall within the past five months.

US Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.7 pts to 43.3%, the 0th percentile over five years and the largest weekly decline since the week of Liberation Day (Apr '25). US Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 8.7 pts to 207.5%, the largest weekly decline since March 2020.

US single stocks saw the largest net selling in more than 4 months (-2.1 SDs 1-year), driven by long and short sales (3.8 to 1). Macro Products (index and ETF) were net bought for a second straight week (+1.5 SDs 1-year).
US-listed ETF shorts rose 7% on Thursday Nov 5, the largest 1-day increase since March and the 3rd largest in 5 years. They rose 3.3% week/week, led by shorting in Large Cap Equity ETFs.

Industrials was the second most net sold global sector, sold for a 4th straight week, with the largest % net selling in over 5 years. Electrical Equipment, Building Products, Aerospace & Defense and Trading Companies & Distributors led the dollar selling, while Passenger Airlines and Machinery were net bought.

GS buyback desk execution mix shifted to 33% open market vs 67% 10b5-1 (prior week 22%/78%) as corporate open windows widen. About 90% of the S&P 500 is in its open window, with about 93% expected by the end of the week.
Desk volumes were 1.6x 2025 YTD ADTV and 1.7x 2024 YTD ADTV, led by Industrials, Financials and Energy. 2026 YTD buyback authorizations reached $1.5T, above the 2025 full-year total of $1.37T.
Overall hedge fund book gross leverage is 314.2% (85th percentile 1-year) while net leverage is 71.8% (4th percentile 1-year). The L/S ratio is 1.592 (3rd percentile 1-year).

Net sold for a 4th straight week with the largest % net selling in over 5 years, driven by long sales and to a lesser extent short sales.

earnings_insights: Q3 reporting is still in progress, and the GS buyback desk says about 90% of S&P 500 companies are in their open window (reported 11/9), with about 93% expected by the end of the week.
risk_factors: CTA selling is concentrated in SPX and grows to $149.5bn over one month if the tape falls.
Hedge fund net leverage is at multi-year lows in the US, and ETF shorting increased sharply, which signals defensive positioning.
vol_and_positioning: CTA flows, 1-week horizon: flat tape -$23.3bn (SPX -$31.1bn), up tape -$3.9bn (SPX -$23.1bn), down tape -$48.7bn (SPX -$31.5bn).
CTA flows, 1-month horizon: flat tape -$45.7bn (SPX -$41.1bn), up tape +$74bn (SPX +$14.4bn), down tape -$149.5bn (SPX -$45.4bn).
SPX key pivot levels: short term 7,676, medium term 7,549, long term 7,084. A 1x standard deviation market move is 1.62% over 1 week and 3.78% over 1 month.
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 4.1 pts to 45.3% (2nd percentile 5-year). Beta-adjusted net leverage fell 7.6 pts to 57.2% (4th percentile 3-year).

The GS Equity Fundamental L/S performance estimate fell 1.48% between 10/30 and 11/5 against MSCI World TR at -3.55%, with beta of -2.07% and alpha of +0.60%. The Systematic L/S estimate fell 0.61%, with alpha of -1% and beta of +0.39%.
Single stocks were net sold for an 8th straight week. Macro Products were net bought for a 3rd straight week globally, driven by long buys and to a lesser extent short covers.
